analysis.one_liner: Cummins India makes diesel and natural gas engines and generator sets, selling to domestic power, industrial and rail customers while exporting engines to its US parent, Cummins Inc.
analysis.whats_happening: Cummins India's board meets around 4 November 2026 to approve September-quarter results - about two weeks from today. The company is also mid-transition on leadership: MD Shveta Arya resigned effective 31 August 2026, and Gbile Adewunmi takes over as MD from 1 November 2026. In the quarter just reported (June 2026), revenue grew a healthy 17.9% year-on-year to ₹3,426 crore, but profit grew only 0.9% because margins fell.
analysis.plain_terms: This is the Indian arm of Cummins, the American engine maker - it builds generators and engines sold both in India and back to its US parent. The business is growing in volume terms: more gensets, more engines, strong domestic demand including from data centres needing backup power. But the money reaching the bottom line isn't growing nearly as fast as sales, because margins slipped in the latest quarter. The stock also trades at a rich price relative to earnings, so it is pricing in more than just steady volume growth - it needs margins to hold up too.
analysis.quarters: Over the last eight quarters (Screener, standalone, ₹ crore revenue/PAT): Sep'24: 2,509/449; Dec'24: 3,096/558; Mar'25: 2,470/530; Jun'25: 2,907/604; Sep'25: 3,170/622; Dec'25: 3,055/486; Mar'26: 3,011/649; Jun'26: 3,426/609. In the June 2026 quarter, revenue rose 17.9% year-on-year but PAT rose just 0.9%, as PAT margin fell from 20.8% to 17.8%. Domestic sales rose 22% and high-horsepower exports rose 37% quarter-on-quarter, but low-horsepower exports fell roughly 20% due to disruption in West Asia/Middle East demand. Management flagged that data centres now account for about 40% of power-generation revenue, up from 23% a year earlier, with a strong order pipeline. A few secondary aggregator sites show slightly different Q1 FY27 figures (revenue ₹3,375 crore, PAT ₹543 crore) versus Screener's ₹3,426 crore/₹609 crore - likely a standalone-vs-consolidated or rounding difference; no evidence of a one-off exceptional item explaining the margin drop. September-quarter (Q2 FY27) results are not yet out.
analysis.performance_read: The stock is down 22.9% from its 27 May 2026 peak of ₹5,977.92 to the current ₹4,608. The only corporate action on record is a share split in September 2011, which is already reflected in historical prices - there has been no recent demerger or spin-off, so this drawdown is a straightforward price correction, not a distortion. Over one year the stock is up 18.4% versus the Nifty's -9.5%, which looks good in isolation. But against its peer Kirloskar Oil Engines (KIRLOSENG), it has badly lagged: +18% vs +131% over 1 year, +180% vs +280% over 3 years, and +444% vs +882% over 5 years. So while Cummins India has beaten the broad market, it has clearly lost the race within its own peer set.
analysis.valuation_read: At roughly 52x earnings and 15x book value, the stock is priced richly for an engine and power-equipment maker. Why it is expensive: the company is effectively debt-free (borrowings of only about ₹37 crore), generates ROE near 30% and ROCE near 40%, and is linked to structural growth themes - data-centre backup power demand and emission-norm (CPCB-IV+) driven replacement cycles. Whether it is actually cheap: no evidence points that way. The latest quarter showed margin compression even as revenue grew, which sits uneasily with a 52x multiple that implicitly assumes both growth and margins hold up.
analysis.growth_read: Growth so far is volume-led - domestic volumes up 22% and overall revenue up 17.9% in the June 2026 quarter - rather than margin-led. That is the more durable kind of growth in principle, but it is undercut here by margin compression (20.8% to 17.8% PAT margin), so the quality of this growth needs the next couple of quarters to confirm whether the margin dip is temporary or a new normal.
analysis.health_read: Balance sheet risk is minimal: the company is net cash, with borrowings of only about ₹37 crore and high returns on capital (ROCE ~40%). The risk here is business/margin risk, not financial risk - specifically, export volatility (Middle East-linked weakness in low-horsepower exports) and sizeable related-party payments, including royalties, to US parent Cummins Inc. Shareholders approved related-party transactions of up to roughly ₹4,093 crore for FY27, which is a meaningful call on the P&L and worth watching as a margin lever.
analysis.ownership_read: Promoter holding (Cummins Inc., USA and related entities) stands at 51%, with no pledging reported. FIIs hold about 19.5% and DIIs about 20.8%, with the remaining roughly 8.7% as public float across about 1.66 lakh shareholders. No prominent individual/celebrity investor appears on the register in available data - if you were expecting one, there isn't one visible here. Governance-wise, note the recent MD transition: Shveta Arya resigned effective 31 August 2026, with Gbile Adewunmi (a long-time Cummins Power Systems executive) set to take over from 1 November 2026, subject to shareholder approval.
strengths: Net cash balance sheet with only about ₹37 crore in borrowings and ROCE near 40%
Revenue grew 17.9% year-on-year in Q1 FY27 (June 2026), with domestic sales up 22%
Data centre-linked genset demand rising fast - 40% of power-generation revenue in Q1 FY27 versus 23% a year earlier
High-horsepower exports up 37% quarter-on-quarter, offsetting weakness in low-horsepower exports
watchpoints: PAT grew only 0.9% year-on-year in Q1 FY27 despite 17.9% revenue growth, as PAT margin fell from 20.8% to 17.8%
Stock has meaningfully lagged peer Kirloskar Oil Engines over 1, 3 and 5 years (+18% vs +131%, +180% vs +280%, +444% vs +882%)
Stock down 22.9% from its May 2026 peak, and a new MD takes charge from 1 November 2026 following the previous MD's resignation
Large related-party/royalty payments to US parent Cummins Inc. (up to ~₹4,093 crore approved for FY27) are a direct draw on margins worth monitoring
analysis.one_thing: The September-quarter (Q2 FY27) results, due around 4 November 2026, will show whether the margin compression seen in Q1 FY27 (PAT margin down to 17.8% from 20.8%) was a one-off or the start of a trend - and the new MD's first commentary should clarify the outlook.
analysis.data_notes: Q1 FY27 revenue/PAT figures were cross-checked against Screener.in (used as primary) against other aggregators showing slightly different numbers (₹3,375 crore/₹543 crore vs ₹3,426 crore/₹609 crore) - likely standalone-vs-consolidated or rounding differences; could not independently verify which is precisely correct. Valuation ratios (P/E ~52x, P/B ~15x, ROE ~30%, ROCE ~40%) and shareholding percentages are from Screener.in as of the September 2026 quarter and a share price close to the supplied ₹4,608. No evidence found of pledging or of a notable individual investor on the shareholder register.
